liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **High Time** (2 reviews): Jerry's vocal on High Time, like China Doll, is called deeply poignant, with a dark 1984 edge; Reviewer says High Time was played only twice in 1984, the other time on 4.27 [24][32]
- **Estimated Prophet** (2 reviews): Reviewer points to Estimated Prophet as where the computer effects can be heard; Jerry plays wild solos, while Bob's vocals run through a processor [31][32]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): The band takes until about Row Jimmy to really gel [33]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Reviewer calls China > Rider ripping, with Jerry wailing on the bridge [32]
- **Turn On Your Love Light** (1 review): Love Light works as an extension of the second set rather than a separate encore [27]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-10-14.168177.beyer.m160.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 25 songs; 182 min [1]
- **gd1984-10-14.132342.Nak100CP4.Hill.Keo.Flac2496**: audience recording; 26 songs; 179 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [3]. Said about its sound: Tape pauses between first set songs and after Samson and Delilah, plus pieces missing at tape flips [3]
- **gd1984-10-14.143829.nak.blend.guy.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 23 songs; 180 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [5]
- **gd84-10-14.nak300.jeffm.3592.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 24 songs; 164 min; rated 4.05/5 by 19 [19]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the audience recording truly superb; Reviewer's old cassette is about as good in quality as this version but lacks the Eyes jam; Audience recording with very good sound, though the reviewer finds the crowd noise distracting [24][26][28][29][33]

## Around the show

- Fire marshal was shutting the show down, so the band hardly left stage before the closer [27]
- Reviewer attended this as their first show, aged 13, and noticed Jerry sitting on a stool [30]
- Reviewer claims this was the first show using computer technology, audible in Estimated Prophet [31]
- No encore was played this night [1]
- No encore was played this night [5]
- Reviewer says the second set especially flows tune into tune with barely a pause, the best example they know [22]
- The dark mood is likened to the Morning Dew from the previous show, 10-12 [24]
- Reviewer doubts the claim that this was the first computer show [30]
- Reviewer sees fall 1984 as ornate, and this show as over the top in setlist and length [33]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-10-14.168177.beyer.m160.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Beyer M160 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [1]
- **gd1984-10-14.132342.Nak100CP4.Hill.Keo.Flac2496**: taped by Steve Hill; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Recorded By Steve Hill, Transfer By Keo; Nakamichi CM100/CP4 Shotguns > Sony D5, Tapes: Maxell UDXLLII 90's; Tapes Labelled: Master-Nakamichi… [3]. Also: Source recorded and shared by Steve, on a Nak100 setup [3]
- **gd1984-10-14.143829.nak.blend.guy.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Mike Guy; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mike Guy's Master Audience Cassettes; 3 mic spread - (2) Nakamichi CM300 mics w/ CP-4 shotgun caps + (1) Nakamichi CM100 mic w/CP-2 omni cap blend > Nakamichi… [5]
- **gd84-10-14.nak300.jeffm.3592.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Cassette Master> DAT> CDR> Eac> SHN; source: FOB> Nakamichi 300's> CP4Cassette Master [19]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1984-10-14 Ticket - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1984-10-14-ticket/) [35]
